newsitem.title: USA: Colombia may resume drug efforts Friday - U.S..
newsitem.headline: Colombia may resume drug efforts Friday - U.S..

text.p: Colombia has told the United States it may resume aerial spraying of illicit drug crops on Friday and "we're pressing them" to do that, the State Department said on Thursday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Colombia explained it had suspended the aerial flights temporarily for "technical reasons" and "hopes to resume the cocoa eradication flights on Friday."
"We hope that's the case and we're pressing them," Burns told reporters.
Colombia quietly suspended the flights on Wednesday after the United States for the second consecutive year refused to certify Colombia as a U.S. ally in the war on illegal narcotics.

Colombia's Cali cartel is alleged to have financed President Ernesto Samper's 1994 election campaign with millions of dollars in drug money. U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette says the cartel's jailed leaders -- Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez -- continue running their empire from behind the walls of Bogota's La Picota prison.
